title: What If All the Ocean's Salt Covered the Land?
subject: ocean salt

scenes.text: What if all the ocean's salt covered the land? It would bury office towers.
Ocean water is about 35 parts per thousand salt, roughly 3.5 percent by weight.
One cubic mile of seawater holds about 120 million tons of salt.
Spread evenly over every continent, it would form a layer more than 500 feet thick.
That's about 166 meters, roughly the height of a 40-story office building.
It all came from rocks on land, washed to the sea by rain and rivers.
